questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to become a professional mathematician at university
Why people fear numbers and whether anyone can manage them
The history of the largest numbers ever written down
Why maths is taught badly in almost every country
questions.why: Sam says they'll explore how the fear of numbers might just be in our heads.

questions.q: How do Neil and Sam feel about maths?
options: Neil loves it, but Sam doesn't
They both enjoyed it at school
Neither of them was good at it
Sam teaches it in his free time
questions.why: Neil says he's not a numbers person, and Sam says 'maybe like me, you weren't good at maths'.

options: It was complicated and not useful in real life
His maths teacher was very strict and unkind
He failed an important maths exam at school
His school friends laughed at his wrong answers
questions.why: He says it was complicated and very theoretical, not practical for real-life situations.

questions.q: According to Charles Seife, why do advertisers and politicians use numbers?
options: Because numbers are easy for people to remember
Because the law says they must
Because numbers make speeches shorter
People rarely question them
questions.why: He says we're primed not to question numbers, so they're powerful tools for deception.

questions.q: Why does Neil give Sam a long, confusing statistic about people who eat meat?
options: To share a real research finding with Sam
To show how hard numbers are to challenge
To test Sam's knowledge of health
To prove that eating meat is unhealthy
questions.why: He says unless you're confident with numbers, you're unlikely to challenge them, then asks if Sam would.

questions.q: What did The Why Factor find about girls and maths?
options: They are worse at maths than boys
They are less interested in numbers
They learn maths faster than boys
They are more anxious, but no worse at it
questions.why: Neil says girls feel more anxious about maths but aren't any worse with numbers.

options: Only some people are born good at numbers
Everyone should study maths at university
Taught well, anyone can learn basic numeracy
Psychology students don't need statistics
questions.why: She says there's no such thing as a numbers person; taught the right way, we can all get basic numeracy.

questions.q: How does Sam feel after hearing Paula Miles?
options: A little better
More anxious than before
Angry about his school
Bored by the topic
questions.why: Sam says, 'I feel a little better now!'
